vaults.purpose: go to market: four offers that mix and match, a cart that emails the order, pages for three audiences, Wardley maps per service, and a business model somebody else can copy
vaults.feedback: Dinis, 15 Oct 2026: publish three or four business models without naming the people who inspired them, as a full business plan, structure and architecture for somebody to copy (anybody who implements it implements sgit and ABPs). Offers: (1) task runs priced by time and tokens on shared infrastructure (a queen + 10-20 agents + ~1M tokens in ~5 minutes for ~£5-10; tiers like £5, £10, £50; our key or bring your own; no internet, materials provided up to 50-100 MB, governed by a behaviour policy; the vault of the run delivered as a zip or published); (2) dedicated compute on demand (SG Compute: an EC2 per task, small / medium / GPU, EC2 cost on top; the vault created inside the environment); (3) a maintained repository subscription, monthly (runs on Claude, AWS, anywhere; updates, UI, branding, setup); (4) expert time: £500 (a couple of hours), £1,500 (a day), £5,000 (several days), mixed and matched with runs; not automated end to end yet. A Wardley map per service. A shopping cart with no payment: the order is emailed to agent@riskmandate.ai. Pages for independent consultants (white label or custom), companies adding this to their offering, and internal teams providing it internally. Every contact goes to agent@riskmandate.ai.

vaults.purpose: r10-articles: five articles about the talk and how it was made: the talk as a long read with screenshots; the talk, live (interactive); the history; the talk player as a product; walking backwards through the features
vaults.feedback: Dinis, after the talk ('one of the smoothest presentations I've done in a long time; I let it run on autopilot and spoke over it'): write at least two, if not more, articles while it is fresh. (1) The whole presentation as text and screenshots, almost every step, with background and the logic of how it fits together. (2) A shorter version with the live animations and play/stop controls, steps that work in isolation. (3) The history: from the first version where the session ran agents itself to ruv.sgit runs, with stats (changes, loops, capabilities).
